_doc: Namibia, written by hand for the ranking and the plans hour by hour (Manu, 2026-11-14). Treks (Fish River Canyon trail) are trail pages of app/trails. Sources per area; scores on docs/RANKING.md.

areas.season: All year. May to October is dry and cool, nights cold in June-August; November to April hot with storms.
areas.sleep: A guesthouse in Klein Windhoek or Ludwigsdorf; pick up the hire car the next morning.
extras: Stock up on groceries and water in Windhoek: out in the country even bread and milk can be hard to find.
Never drive at night: wildlife on the roads. Gravel eats tyres: check the spare before you leave.

items.name: Windhoek centre: the Christuskirche and the Independence Museum
items.why: The German church of 1910 on its hill, and the museum of the struggle for independence next to it, with the view from its top-floor café.

items.name: Daan Viljoen nature reserve
items.why: Walking trails among zebra, kudu and oryx in the Khomas hills, twenty minutes from town.

items.name: Dinner at Joe's Beer House
items.why: Windhoek's famous beer garden: game meat on the grill, the first night's ritual of every self-drive trip.

areas.season: All year. May to September the days are mild and the nights near freezing; December to February over 40°C at midday.
areas.sleep: Inside the park gate (Sesriem campsite or Sossus Dune Lodge, booked with Namibia Wildlife Resorts): only from there you are on the dunes at sunrise. Lodges outside wait for the gate to open.
extras: The road from Sesriem is 65 km, tarred except the last 5 km of deep sand: leave the hire car at the 2x4 car park and take the 4x4 shuttle.
Carry more water than you think: two litres each for the morning.

items.name: Sunrise on Dune 45, then Deadvlei and Sossusvlei
items.best: From the gate at sunrise, out by 11:30
items.book: Park permit at the Sesriem office; stay inside the gate to start before sunrise.
items.why: The red dunes of the world's oldest desert at first light, and the white pan of Deadvlei with camel-thorn trees dead for 600 years, under dunes up to 400 m: the picture of Namibia.

steps.what: Drive from Sesriem toward the dunes
steps.note: 45 km to Dune 45, the gate opens at sunrise

steps.what: Climb Dune 45, 170 m of sand, for the sunrise
steps.note: about an hour up the ridge

steps.what: On to the 2x4 car park, 4x4 shuttle the last 5 km
Walk across the sand to Deadvlei
steps.note: the trees in shadow, the dunes lit

steps.what: Back to Sesriem before the midday heat

items.name: Big Daddy, the dune over Deadvlei
items.best: Start at the gate's opening: by 10:00 the sand burns
items.why: The tallest dune around Deadvlei, over 300 m of soft sand up the ridge, then a run straight down into the white pan.

items.name: Sesriem Canyon at sunset
items.why: A narrow gorge 4 km from the gate: climb down and walk the dry riverbed, the old water place of the Dorsland trekkers.

items.name: A hot-air balloon over the Namib at sunrise
items.book: Book ahead from Sesriem or Solitaire; flights go only on still mornings.
items.why: An hour floating over the dunes and the gravel plains, landing for a champagne breakfast.

areas.season: All year, but cool and often foggy: the cold Benguela current keeps the coast at 15-25°C while the desert behind is hot. Bring a fleece.
areas.sleep: Swakopmund, the old German town: cafés, a beach and the base for every tour.

rain.name: Swakopmund's museums and cafés
rain.why: The Kristall Galerie with the world's largest quartz crystal, the aquarium, coffee and cake in the German bakeries.

items.name: Sandwich Harbour by 4x4, where the dunes meet the ocean
items.book: Only with a tour from Walvis Bay or Swakopmund: the track needs special vehicles.
items.why: Dunes over 100 m falling straight into the Atlantic, a lagoon of flamingos, and a drive along the beach that only works at low tide.

steps.what: Walvis Bay lagoon: flamingos and pelicans
South along the beach between the dunes and the surf
Up on the dunes over Sandwich Harbour's lagoon
Back to Walvis Bay, often by the dunes

items.name: Dolphin and seal cruise in Walvis Bay
items.why: Pelican Point's seals climbing on the boat, dolphins, whales in season, and oysters with sparkling wine on deck.

items.name: Swakopmund: the old town and the jetty at sunset
items.why: Half-timbered houses of German South West Africa, the Woermannhaus tower, and the 300 m jetty into the Atlantic at sunset.

items.name: Spitzkoppe, the Matterhorn of Namibia
items.why: A granite peak of 1,728 m alone on the plain, a rock arch, and San paintings that a local guide shows you.

items.name: Sandboarding on Dune 7
items.why: Down the dunes on a board, standing or head-first on your belly; a quad takes you back up.

items.name: The Moon Landscape and the welwitschia plants
items.why: Eroded hills like a lunar surface, and welwitschia, a desert plant that lives over a thousand years.

items.name: Cape Cross seal colony
items.why: Up to 100,000 Cape fur seals on the rocks where a Portuguese navigator raised a stone cross in 1486; the noise and the smell are part of it.

areas.season: May to October, dry and mild. Summer is very hot.
areas.sleep: A lodge or community camp near Twyfelfontein, among the red rocks.

items.name: Twyfelfontein's rock engravings and the Organ Pipes
items.book: Visits only with the site's guide, included in the ticket; tip the guide.
items.why: One of the largest groups of rock engravings in Africa, over 2,500 carved by hunter-gatherers and herders over thousands of years: a UNESCO site. Then the basalt columns of the Organ Pipes nearby.

steps.what: The Organ Pipes, a short walk into a gully
Back to the lodge for the hot hours

items.name: Desert elephants in the dry riverbeds
items.why: Elephants that live in the desert, walking the dry rivers of Damaraland; a lodge guide knows where they are today.

items.name: The White Lady rock painting of the Brandberg
items.best: Start early: the gorge is hot by midday
items.book: Permit at the Brandberg rest camp in Uis or the National Heritage Council in Windhoek.
items.why: A guided walk into Namibia's highest mountain to a painting at least 2,000 years old; despite the name, a male shaman.

items.name: The Petrified Forest
items.why: Tree trunks up to 45 m long turned to stone, with welwitschia growing among them.

areas.season: May to October, the dry months: the animals gather at the waterholes. November to April green and hot, animals spread out, birds arrive.
areas.sleep: Inside the park, at the Okaukuejo, Halali or Namutoni rest camps: the floodlit waterholes are by your room after the gates close.
extras: You drive yourself on good gravel, no 4x4 needed, 60 km/h. Gates close at sunset: be back in camp.
Crossing the park east to west takes most of a day.

items.name: A day of waterholes by car
items.best: Out at the gate's opening, a break at midday, out again from 15:30
items.book: Park permit at the gate and the camp office; pay for all the days in one go.
items.why: Elephants, giraffes, zebra and springbok queueing to drink, lions waiting nearby: you drive from one waterhole to the next at your pace.

steps.what: Leave camp at sunrise, the gates open
The waterholes near camp: lions often still there
Back to camp for the hot hours, pool and lunch
Out again: the best time for animals at the water
Back before the gate closes at sunset

items.name: Okaukuejo's floodlit waterhole at night
items.why: A bench by the fence, a drink and binoculars: elephants, black rhinos and lions come to drink under the lights.

items.name: The Etosha Pan viewpoints
items.why: A white salt pan to the horizon, shimmering with mirages; after a good rain, flamingos.

items.name: A guided drive at dawn or at night
items.why: An open vehicle from the camp, out before the gates open or after dark, when the cats hunt.

areas.season: May to October; a sedan reaches Opuwo, a 4x4 for the villages and beyond.
areas.sleep: A lodge on the hill above Opuwo.
extras: Ask before every photo, and never photograph people in their homestead without their yes: respect is the deal.

items.name: A Himba village with a local guide
items.why: The OvaHimba keep their way of life: ochre-red skin, leather and huts of mud and dung. A guide from the community explains, translates and asks first.

items.name: Opuwo's market and streets
items.why: Himba, Herero in Victorian dresses and townspeople side by side: one of the most striking towns in Africa.

areas.season: After the rains, March to June, the falls are fullest; the road from Opuwo is long and rough.
areas.sleep: A lodge or camp on the Kunene, under the palms by the falls.
extras: The Kunene has crocodiles and hippos: do not swim, and keep away from the bank outside the settlement.

items.name: Epupa Falls at sunset from the hill
items.why: The Kunene splits into dozens of channels over 1.5 km, drops of up to 37 m between baobabs and palms, on the border with Angola.

items.name: A guided walk along the Kunene
items.why: Birds, crocodiles from a safe distance, and the Himba homesteads of the valley with a guide from the lodge.

areas.season: March to October. Summer passes 40°C in the canyon.
areas.sleep: Hobas camp or a lodge near the canyon rim.
extras: The five-day trail through the canyon is on its trail page: only March to September, with a doctor's certificate and a group of three or more.

items.name: Sunset over the Fish River Canyon from Hobas
items.why: Africa's largest canyon, 550 m deep and 160 km long: from the main viewpoint the river bends in the rock below.

items.name: Along the rim from viewpoint to viewpoint
items.why: The canyon from one bend to the next on the edge, without going down.

areas.season: July to November, when the bush dries and the animals come to the river. The rains (December-March) bring mud and mosquitoes: malaria area.
areas.sleep: A lodge on the Kavango river near Divundu.

items.name: Game drive in Mahango
items.why: Buffalo, sable and roan antelope, elephants and hippos on the Okavango floodplain: the green Namibia, nothing like the desert.

items.name: A sunset boat on the Kavango
items.why: Hippos, crocodiles and hundreds of birds from a small boat, the sun going down over the reeds.
